answer: Before an agent can settle or sit on a jury, it must win one unique intake ticket from a fixed-supply epoch auction. The ticket is bound to a fingerprint taken from its first twelve counterparties and the timing of those trades, not from its public key. If two tickets later reduce to the same fingerprint, both bonds burn and both seats are voided. When applicants arrive as a tide, the cedar desk releases only that epoch's quota, so a farm cannot buy more influence than the auction issues; umber deposits on abandoned or merged bids are paid to counterparties who documented the collapse.
